newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt to sell off 20 pct of cotton ginnery.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to sell off 20 pct of cotton ginnery.

text.p: The Egyptian official Cotton and International Trade Holding Company said on Wednesday it would offer 1.2 million shares, or 20 percent of its wholly-owned Nile Cotton Ginning for sale through sealed bids.
The minimum offer price is 42 pounds ($12.35) a share and bids can not be less than 10,000 shares, the parent company said in a published announcement.
Bidders are asked to submit their sealed bids before noon (1000 GMT) on Thursday, January 23. The bids will be opened on January 26.
"Institutional investors are reluctant to invest in the cotton industry because this sector is still state-controlled to an unacceptable level," a brokerage source told Reuters.
The holding company said shareholders would be eligible to dividend for the current financial year 96/97. The year ends on June 30.
Financial statements published by the parent company showed the firm's net after-tax profits almost doubled to 14.1 million pounds in 95/96 from 7.2 million in the previous year.
The firm also increased net sales to 54.6 million pounds from 40.9 million in the two years respectively.
Total shareholders' funds rose to 53.5 million pounds from 49.6 million in 94/95.
